agree.reason: A wary fixed-income retiree gets a plain, respectful case: an exact $10-a-month cost, a fixed rate and end date against the 'blank check' letter, and the local branch closing in July, though the script gives no stronger reason why this vote should differ from the last one.

honest.reason: Every figure checks out ($640k × 0.19/1,000 ≈ $122/yr ≈ $10/mo; $410k ≈ $78/yr), and the script drops the misleading coffee line, but 'for most homes here' stretches a median figure a little.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly turns the rate into Ridgeview and citywide monthly and yearly costs, but it never gives smaller true forms such as about $2.30 a week or 33 cents a day, and it never connects the $2.3M a year to the cost of each service.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated concretely and correctly (the Ridgeview branch closes in July and Sunday hours are not restored), and the 22% rise in visits is set against it as the trend.

qualification.reason: A door script stating a fixed rate, term and closure date needs no hedge.

objections.reason: The 'blank check' and fixed-income objections are met directly with the brief's facts and an honest admission of the cost, though the reply to 'the last one failed' says little to persuade.

fit.reason: It fits on one card with a 60–90 second core and short rebuttals, but it leaves out the coffee comparison the field lead asked for without a note explaining why.
